title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has issued a formal response to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining its approach to ensuring AI technologies meet national values and public expectations. In its reply, the government details plans for policy development, regulatory oversight, and collaborative efforts to establish robust AI standards across industry and public services.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has outlined its strategy for overseeing how AI is used in qualifications, aiming to ensure fairness, reliability and transparency in assessments. The approach involves setting guidelines and monitoring mechanisms to protect the integrity of qualifications while fostering responsible AI adoption.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected works are used to train and develop AI systems, analyzing the legal, ethical, and economic effects of such practices. It offers an impact assessment and recommends ways to balance creators’ rights with the advancement of AI technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its plans to tackle the concerns raised about artificial intelligence. It highlights measures to improve AI safety, boost innovation, and strengthen regulation, while stressing the importance of working together with industry, academia and the public.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the purpose, scope, and duties of the committee that will review how artificial intelligence affects public standards, including rules on data use, transparency, and accountability. It also answers common questions about the committee’s goals, expected results, and how it will involve stakeholders.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into how Artificial Intelligence should be governed. Their submission highlights key governance issues, including regulatory frameworks, risk mitigation, and best‑practice recommendations for AI oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document examines how the growing use of AI is changing rules and oversight for medical products, ensuring safety and effectiveness. It outlines steps to apply the AI White Paper’s principles to the regulatory framework for medical devices and drugs.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines the government's plan to make the defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI user among nations of similar size. It focuses on developing, integrating and governing AI capabilities across defence operations to achieve these goals while ensuring safety and accountability.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Department for Transport explains how it will partner with the transport sector to take advantage of opportunities that artificial intelligence offers. It also details steps the government will take to manage and minimise the risks that AI can bring.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used to train and develop AI systems, assessing compliance with legal requirements. It evaluates progress made under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act and outlines steps for ensuring lawful use of copyrighted content in AI development.
